intro.summary: Turn a race result or target time into useful, easy-to-understand performance information. Built for athletes, parents and coaches.
intro.sideBody: No account needed. Choose what you want to calculate, enter your details and see the result.

disclaimer: A note about your results. RUN-LAB calculators use mathematical formulas and performance models to calculate or estimate running times, paces, speeds and performance comparisons. Results are intended as a guide, not a guarantee of future performance. Actual results may vary depending on fitness, training, pacing, fatigue, terrain, weather and race-day conditions.

predict.title: Predict my times at other distances
predict.description: Use a current PB to estimate equivalent race performances.
predict.purpose:
Imagine Sarah has a 1500m PB of 5:30. What might she run for 3000m?

She can enter one PB for a prediction, or add a second PB, such as her 5000m time, to make the estimate more personal.

Think of it like joining two dots on a graph rather than guessing from one.

It's a useful guide, not a guarantee.
predict.formLead: Enter a PB, optionally add another PB, then choose the target distance.

pace.title: Calculate my race pace
pace.description: Turn a distance and finishing time into pace and speed.
pace.purpose:
James has just run 1500m in 5:30. But how fast was he actually running?

Enter a distance and finishing time to discover your average pace, speed and split times.

It's like breaking a race into smaller, easier-to-understand pieces.

Remember, these are averages. Your pace may have varied throughout the race.
pace.formLead: Enter a race distance and finishing time to see your average pace, speed and splits.

finish.title: Calculate my finishing time
finish.description: Enter a distance and running pace to find your finish time.
finish.purpose:
Sophie wants to run 3000m at 4 minutes per kilometre. What finishing time would that give her?

Enter your distance and target pace to find out. For Sophie, that's 12 minutes.

It's like planning a journey. Know the distance and speed, and you can calculate the time.

The result assumes a steady average pace. It's a calculation, not a prediction of your fitness.
finish.formLead: Enter a race distance and pace to calculate the finishing time.

target.title: Plan my target PB
target.description: See the pace and splits needed to reach your next goal.
target.purpose:
Omar has a 1500m PB of 5:10. His next goal is to break 5 minutes. But what pace does he need to run?

Enter your target distance and finishing time to discover the pace and splits needed to reach your goal.

Think of it like planning a journey. Rather than just knowing where you want to finish, you can see the checkpoints along the way.

It's a pacing plan, not a guarantee. The hard work still happens on the track.
target.formLead: Enter the distance and target PB time to see the pace and even splits you need.

splits.title: Build my race splits
splits.description: Create clear checkpoint times for your chosen race.
splits.purpose:
Javier wants to run 800m in 2:20. Should he run both laps at exactly the same speed?

Choose your race distance, target time and pacing strategy to build a set of race splits.

Think of it like having a race map. Each checkpoint tells you where you should be, helping you judge your effort and stay on track.

Your splits are a guide. Real races rarely go exactly to plan.
splits.formLead: Enter your race distance and goal finishing time to build checkpoint times. Choose even pace or a 2% negative split, and how often to mark the race.

profile.title: Discover my performance profile
profile.description: Compare your performances and discover where your running strengths currently lie.
profile.purpose:
Layla runs 800m, 1500m and 3000m. But which is actually her strongest event?

Enter your personal bests to compare your performances using World Athletics points.

You might be good at 800m, better at 1500m and strongest at 3000m. But how can you tell when the distances are so different? That's where the points come in.

Discover your strengths, spot opportunities and see where you might improve next.

It's a snapshot of where you are today, not a limit on what you can achieve tomorrow.
profile.formLead: Enter 2–6 race performances to compare them on the World Athletics scale and see whether your results currently lean towards speed, middle-distance or endurance.

ageGrade.title: Age-grade my performance
ageGrade.description: See how good a race is when age and sex are taken into account.
ageGrade.purpose:
Pat is 45 and has just run 5K in 22 minutes. But how good is that performance for someone of Pat's age?

Enter your age, sex, race distance and finishing time to discover your age-grade percentage.

Think of it like giving everyone a fairer starting point. A 60-year-old and a 25-year-old might run different times, but both could produce equally impressive performances for their age.

You'll also see an equivalent time showing how your performance compares with an open-age runner.

It's a way to celebrate what you can do at your age, not just how fast you run.
ageGrade.formLead: Enter sex, age, distance and race time to see your age-grade percentage on the 2025 road standards.
